unit.title: Earth and Sky
unit.blurb: Weather changes from day to day. The Sun gives us light, and it is day when our side of the Earth faces the Sun.
unit.subject: science

O2.t: Know that the Sun gives light and that we have day and night.

p: The **weather** can be **sunny**, **rainy**, **cloudy**, **windy** or **snowy**. It changes from day to day, so we choose clothes to match.
Draw the weather every day for a week. Which weather did you see most?

p: The **Sun** is a star. It gives us **light** and warmth. In the **day** our part of the Earth faces the Sun, so it is light. At **night** our part faces away, so it is dark.
The Sun is so bright it can hurt your eyes. Never look straight at it.

q.prompt: What gives us light in the daytime?

options.fb: The Moon shines at night but is much dimmer.
A torch is small; the Sun lights up the whole sky.

q.prompt: When can you usually see the stars?

options.fb: The Sun is too bright in the day.

options.fb: Playing in the park is day.

req.reason: Sun in the sky is day.

req.prompt: Put the times of day in order.
req.reason: The Sun rises in the morning, is high in the afternoon, sets in the evening, and then it is night.

req.prompt: Which word means: the star that gives us light?
req.reason: Sun means the star that gives us light.

options.fb: Day means when it is light.
Night means when it is dark.
